Morphism of topoi $f\colon\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$: a pair of functors with an adjunction,
f^*\colon \mathcal F\to\mathcal E\ \dashv\ f_*\colon \mathcal E\to\mathcal F,\qquad f^*\ \text{left exact (finite inverse limits)}
$\operatorname{Hom}(V,U)$ in $\mathcal O_Y$: empty or one point; $\varinjlim_{V\ni y'}\operatorname{Hom}(V,U)\neq\varnothing\iff y'\in U$.
Category of fibre functors = the set $Y$ ordered by specialization; points: the opposite order.
$f,g\colon X\to Y$ continuous; $\operatorname{Hom}(f,g)$ has at most one element, and
Necessity: for $x\colon P\to X$, a 2-morphism $\alpha\colon f\Rightarrow g$ gives $\alpha * x\colon f\circ x\Rightarrow g\circ x$, i.e. $f(x)\to g(x)$.
Uniqueness: $f^*F\to g^*F$ is determined on fibres at every $x$; $\operatorname{Top}(X)$ has enough points (conservative family of fibre functors).
Existence: the morphisms on fibres $(f^*F)_x\to(g^*F)_x$ assemble to a morphism of sheaves.

\operatorname{Top}(X,G),\qquad (X,G)\to(X',G'):\ X\to X',\ G\to G'\ \text{compatible with the actions}
Y=Y'\times_{X'}X\ \subset\ X\times Y',\qquad Y'\ \text{étale over } X' \text{ with } G'\text{-action}
$G$ acts diagonally on $X\times Y'$ (through $G\to G'$ on $Y'$); $Y$ is stable.
